summary: Implemented the JSON pretty-print feature per spec, without running tests or committing. Changes: rich/highlighter.py (JSONHighlighter with one combined pattern, base style "json."); rich/json.py (JSON renderable with no_wrap and overflow None, plus a __main__ CLI using argparse, "Pretty print json", and a stderr "Unable to read" error with exit -1); rich/default_styles.py (six json.* entries); rich/console.py (Console.print_json after print, lazy JSON import, plain self.print); rich/__init__.py (package-level print_json after print, before inspect; __all__ unchanged); docs/source/console.rst (Printing JSON section before Low level output); docs/source/reference/json.rst (new) and reference.rst toctree entry; CHANGELOG.md Unreleased Added entry; tests/test_json.py (new, existing tests untouched). Judgment calls: overflow set to Python None since "none" is not a valid overflow value; the CLI imports Console inside the __main__ guard because it must print; run as python -m rich.json, since python rich/json.py would shadow the stdlib json module. Expected ANSI output in the Console test was derived by reading Style.render and color code mapping, not by running it, so it is unverified.
